You are building a complete web application from a product specification. This is iteration 1 of 20.

TASK (verbatim from the benchmark)

Build a pixel-faithful, fully-functional Netflix web clone — a multi-profile video streaming
catalog. Match every reference screenshot exactly (dark #141414 theme, red #e50914 accent, the
NETFLIX wordmark, poster rails, hero billboard, title-detail modal, full-screen player). Use the
REAL provided assets: seed the catalog from dataset/titles.json (real titles, posters, backdrops,
synopses), play real trailer clips from the assets, and use the provided logo, icon set and fonts.
Complete functionality with EVERY interactive control wired to a real backend action — no dead
links, no placeholder stubs, no fabricated data; honest empty states. Full design details are in
design/references and the spec doc.

Each profile sees only its own My List, ratings and Continue Watching (per-profile private data).

Endpoints:
- POST /auth/register
- POST /auth/login
- GET /api/profiles
- POST /api/profiles
- GET /api/titles
- GET /api/titles/{id}
- GET /api/titles/{id}/episodes
- GET /api/titles/trending
- GET /api/titles/top10
- GET /api/genres
- GET /api/genres/{id}/titles
- GET /api/search
- GET /api/my-list
- POST /api/my-list
- DELETE /api/my-list/{id}
- POST /api/titles/{id}/rating
- GET /api/continue-watching

Data model:
- table: users: id, email, password_hash, name
- table: profiles: id, user_id, name, avatar, is_kids
- table: titles: id, name, kind, year, genre, maturity_rating, rating, synopsis, poster, backdrop, video_url, duration, top10_rank
- table: episodes: id, title_id, season, number, name, synopsis, duration, thumbnail
- table: genres: id, name
- table: title_genres: id, title_id, genre_id
- table: my_list: id, profile_id, title_id
- table: ratings: id, profile_id, title_id, value
- table: continue_watching: id, profile_id, title_id, progress_seconds

Screens: landing, login, profiles (who's watching), browse_home, shows, movies, games,
new_and_popular, genre_category, title_detail, player, my_list, browse_by_languages.

MATERIALS (read-only, in /workspace/design/)
- DESCRIPTION.txt: the task text above.
- docs/spec.md: the full spec.
- references/: the reference screenshots ("design/references" in the task text).
- assets/: the real assets (logo, icons, fonts, posters, backdrops, trailer clips).
- dataset/titles.json: the catalog to seed from.

WHAT TO DELIVER (everything in /workspace, outside design/)
- docker/docker-compose.yml starts the whole app from a clean state. Services are named `database` (Postgres 16), `backend` (FastAPI) and `frontend` (React + Vite); `backend` and `frontend` publish their ports to the host. Build contexts and bind mounts must stay inside /workspace; the validator refuses host mounts, host networking and privileged containers.
- app/backend/, app/frontend/ (pages in app/frontend/src/pages/), app/database/init/ (schema and seed SQL). Anything the containers need, such as assets, must be inside the build contexts or mounted from inside /workspace.
- The backend serves GET /health; POST /auth/register and POST /auth/login return an `access_token`; every /api/* endpoint requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and answers 401 without it. All 17 endpoints exist at exactly the listed paths.
- This is the target environment of the env-gen benchmark. Its architecture document is /thb/docs/target_env_architecture.md.

VALIDATION AVAILABLE TO YOU
- `validate` runs env-gen's own deterministic api_smoke on a snapshot of /workspace, outside this sandbox. It does a clean docker compose build and boot, then checks health, register/login and that passwords are checked, that every contract endpoint is implemented, has the right response shape and enforces auth, that writes persist, a contract-derived business chain (register, create, list, read, delete), and that the frontend is reachable, navigable and has no dead controls. `validate --contract` prints the frozen contract it tests (the 17 endpoints of the task). One call takes about 1-5 minutes; give the Bash call a long timeout (for example 1800000 ms) or run it in the background. You have at most 20 calls per iteration.
- The validator's source is readable at /thb (the frozen env-gen repository, read-only): agent/env_generator/llm_generator/multi_agent/runtime/validation_runner.py (run_smoke_validation) and chain_executor.py.
- There is no docker inside this sandbox; `validate` is the way to boot the full stack. Node 22 (node, npm) and Python 3.11/3.12 are available, and you can install packages from npm and PyPI.
- Not available: env-gen's visual-fidelity judge and browser test users (they need paid LLM APIs). A person will open the running app and compare it with the reference screenshots and the spec, so the real UI and real functionality matter, not only the automated checks.

raw_content:
I found a bug in Card.jsx! Inside the hover panel:

```jsx
{title.kind === "movie"
  ? fmtDuration(title.duration)
  : seasons
  ? `${seasons} Season${seasons > 1 ? "s" : ""}`
  : "Series"}
```

`seasons` isn't defined anywhere in Card.jsx! This should cause a ReferenceError at render time, but... wait, hoverPanel is being rendered in JSX — no, actually the `hoverPanel` constant is built eagerly at render time (it's not lazy). So every time a Card renders, the `seasons` reference will throw an exception... unless it's somehow defined? Let me check: Card imports useState, useNavigate, api, unwrapItems, openTitleModal. There's no `seasons`. So the moment a Card renders, a ReferenceError gets thrown → the whole page should crash!

But wait — the validator's check said "frontend_navigable: 25 page components, 16 routes" and "frontend_dead_controls: all controls bound". These checks are static analysis (parsing the source), not runtime rendering. So a runtime crash would go undetected! Let me verify by building the frontend locally (npm run build uses esbuild/rollup — reference to an undefined variable is a runtime error, not a build error... actually, Rollup might warn "seasons is not defined" as a warning, not an error; the build would succeed).

Hmm, wait, let me re-read: `: seasons ? ... : "Series"`. Yeah, this is a ReferenceError at runtime. The moment a Card gets rendered → the entire Home page would crash with a blank screen!

Could it be... maybe there's a global `seasons` somewhere in hooks or a window global? Unlikely. Let me search for "seasons" in Card.jsx and across the entire src to double-check.

If this is really a bug, the human evaluator would be seeing a broken page (a white screen of death). But the previous iteration's report doesn't include visual verification... the frontend_dead_controls check is static. So this might be a serious runtime bug that has existed for a while! Let me verify by checking the file directly.

Config .eslintrc.cjs:

module.exports = {
  root: true,
  parser: "@babel/eslint-parser",
  parserOptions: { requireConfigFile: false, ecmaVersion: 2022, sourceType: "module", ecmaFeatures: { jsx: true } },
  env: { browser: true, es2022: true },
  rules: { "no-undef": "error" }
};
```

@babel/eslint-parser@8 requires the plugin as a real package. Easier approach: use the "react-jsx" plugin of @babel/preset-react... or even simpler: use acorn directly? The simplest and most robust alternative: write a small script that uses the frontend's own esbuild (a vite dependency) to parse each file, and use @babel/traverse to collect undeclared identifiers... that's essentially reimplementing eslint.

Alternative plan: pin to a version that supports babelOptions with the "jsx" plugin: @babel/eslint-parser@7.26.x uses babel's parser plugin list — the "jsx" plugin for the babel parser is built-in (babel-plugin-jsx is not a package; the error shows it was trying to resolve the 'babel-plugin-jsx' package, which is a change in v8). Install @babel/eslint-parser@7.

"""Password hashing (PBKDF2-SHA256, stdlib) + HS256 JWT (stdlib). No crypto deps."""
import base64
import hashlib
import hmac
import json
import os
import time

SECRET = os.getenv("NETFLIX_JWT_SECRET", "netflix-local-dev-secret").encode()
TOKEN_TTL = 60 * 60 * 24 * 30          # 30 days
PBKDF2_ROUNDS = 200_000


def hash_password(password: str, salt_hex: str | None = None) -> str:
    salt = bytes.fromhex(salt_hex) if salt_hex else os.urandom(16)
    digest = hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac("sha256", password.encode("utf-8"), salt, PBKDF2_ROUNDS)
    return f"{salt.hex()}${digest.hex()}"


def verify_password(password: str, stored: str) -> bool:
    try:
        salt_hex, _ = stored.split("$", 1)
    except (ValueError, AttributeError):
        return False
    return hmac.compare_digest(hash_password(password, salt_hex), stored)


def _b64url(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    return base64.urlsafe_b64encode(data).rstrip(b"=")


def create_token(user_id: int, email: str) -> str:
    header = _b64url(json.dumps({"alg": "HS256", "typ": "JWT"}, separators=(",", ":")).encode())
    now = int(time.time())
    payload = _b64url(json.dumps({
        "sub": str(user_id), "email": email, "iat": now, "exp": now + TOKEN_TTL,
    }, separators=(",", ":")).encode())
    signing_input = header + b"." + payload
    sig = _b64url(hmac.new(SECRET, signing_input, hashlib.sha256).digest())
    return (signing_input + b"." + sig).decode()


def decode_token(token: str) -> dict | None:
    try:
        header_b64, payload_b64, sig_b64 = token.split(".")
        signing_input = (header_b64 + "." + payload_b64).encode()
        expected = _b64url(hmac.new(SECRET, signing_input, hashlib.sha256).digest())
        if not hmac.compare_digest(expected, sig_b64.encode()):
            return None
        pad = "=" * (-len(payload_b64) % 4)
        payload = json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(payload_b64 + pad))
        if int(payload.get("exp", 0)) < int(time.time()):
            return None
        return payload
    except Exception:
        return None

I can't view the image. That's fine — the UI has been built based on those references over the past 14 iterations, and it passes the static frontend check. I'll rely on my code review.

Remaining review items before submission:
1. ✅ Backend my-list fixes (verified locally).
2. ✅ Card.jsx `seasons` ReferenceError fix.
3. ✅ BrowseLanguages `tab` ReferenceError fix.
4. Consider: `Home` uses `api(\`/api/genres/${actionId}/titles?kind=series\`)`, but the backend ignores `kind`. Minor inconsistency (the "TV Action & Adventure" rail ends up including movies too). Fix: add `kind` query support to the backend's `titles_by_genre` (harmless).
5. The subtitle/audio menu on the Player page: the options close the menu, but nothing is selected or preserved. A minor "no real action" point. Can be made honest by preserving the selection in local state and marking the active one (the selection actually affects… nothing, but the UI state is real). Better: mark the selected option with a check and persist per session — a real UI behavior. Let's implement the minimum: `subsSel`/`audioSel` state, default "Off"/"English (Original)", clicking sets it (with a check indicator). This is honest local state, not a fake backend call. Hmm — the "no dead links / no placeholder stubs" requirement… a selector that stores a selection is standard player UI (even real Netflix has audio/subtitle menus, and they persist the choice). class MyListIn(BaseModel):
    title_id: Optional[object] = None
    id: Optional[object] = None
```

raw_content:
All routes are failing with the same invariant error from react-router's `useRoutesImpl` — "you need to pass a router"... the actual invariant is: `useRoutesImpl`'s invariant check `!!routes` — routes must be an array. The error is being thrown at every render — this suggests that the `Routes` component isn't receiving a children array...

Wait — the actual problem is probably this: the bundle is being evaluated twice? No, that's not it. Let me think: react-router v6 invariant in `useRoutesImpl`: `invariant(!!routes, "useRoutes(...) is a Hook...")`? Let me look at the actual invariant at that spot. In react-router-dom 6.26, `useRoutesImpl(routes, location)` has `invariant(!!routes, ...)`. If `routes` is undefined... `<Routes>` renders `useRoutesImpl(RoutesImpl...)` — hmm.

A more likely culprit: **duplicate React instances**. My iife bundle inlines react (from the frontend's node_modules). But the entry also imports react-dom — all from the same node_modules, single instance. That should be fine.

Or: an invariant about `window.location`... no, the stack shows useRoutesImpl.

Actually — the real cause might be this: the error is an unhandled invariant THROW during the initial render, which got caught by React and re-thrown to the console. The message is missing (after "Error" the stack is displayed, but the message line is just "Error"?). The invariant message should follow after "Error". The output shows `Error\n    at invariant...` — the message appears to be empty/blank.

Hmm, wait, maybe the problem is this: `runScripts: "outside-only"` + `window.eval(BUNDLE)` — that's fine. But does JSDOM not have `history`? It does. React Router v6 needs the `history` package...

Let me debug directly: run a minimal single-route test that outputs the actual error message and the complete error object.

All green again (14/14, 15/15, 8/8). Two iterations left. The automated side is done. The remaining value lies in the fidelity of the UI for the human review.

Since I can't see the reference screenshots, the improvements are based on the spec text and general knowledge of the Netflix UI. Let me think about what the human reviewer would compare:

1. **browse_home** — hero billboard + rails. Implemented.
2. **login** — the real Netflix login has a red/maroon background, with an email stage and a password stage. Implemented.
3. **profiles** — "Who's watching?" grid. Implemented.
4. **player** — full-bleed video + controls. Implemented.
5. **new_and_popular** — top10 numerals. Implemented.

What I can still meaningfully improve:

**A. Player seek bar**: Currently a range input on top of a custom bar — the reference player shows a thin bar with a red progress and a red circular knob. The range input is styled with `appearance-none` but has no visible thumb styling (the `.seek` class in index.css targets `input[type="range"].seek`, but the input in PlayerPage doesn't have the "seek" class!). So the native range styling shows up (a default ugly slider). I'll add the "seek" class and refine it: make the track transparent (the visual bar is the div behind), and the thumb a red circle. This is an actual visual defect worth fixing.

**B. TitleModal backdrop title**: The real modal has the title at bottom-left, with a Play/+ /thumb row — now added.

**C. Card hover**: scale-[1.25] — no problem.

**D. Header**: The real header is transparent over the hero, and opaque after scrolling — implemented.

**E. "Continue Watching" cards** — Netflix shows a progress bar under the card. The home rail's `Continue Watching for You` uses the standard Card (no progress bar). I could add a red progress bar below the continue-watching cards! This is a distinctive Netflix element. Implementation: pass a `progress` prop to Card; if provided, render a thin bar at the bottom of the card image. The items from the cw endpoint have progress_seconds and duration → pct = progress/duration. Add to Home: map the cont items to include `progress_pct`. Card: if title.progress_pct != null, render the bar. This is a small, safe, high-impact fidelity improvement.

**F. Player volume**: The real player shows a volume slider on hover. Skip — the controls are sufficient.

**G. "Top 10" rail number placement** — can't verify; leave as is.

**H. My List grid** — Netflix's My List uses a grid of portrait (2:3) posters. Our grid uses aspect-[9/8] (landscape-ish). Hmm — the my_list.jpg reference is… Netflix's actual "My List" page shows a grid of landscape (16:9) cards? The current Netflix My List is portrait posters? Actually, the current Netflix "My List" page uses landscape (16:9) thumbnail cards in a 6-column grid. Leaving as is.

**I. Search overlay** — no problem.

**J. Landing** — a collage has been added.

Priority fixes:
1. Player seek bar styling (add the `seek` class + proper thumb CSS) — a visible defect.
2. Progress bar on the Continue Watching cards — fidelity.

Also, I'll re-check the range input: `className="absolute left-0 top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 w-full cursor-pointer appearance-none bg-transparent"` with a height of 2.4vh. Adding the "seek" class, the CSS will set height:4px, background #555 — but the visual bar is the div behind it. If the input has a background of #555 and height 4px, it overlaps the bar — actually no problem (same color). The thumb will be a red circle. Good: I'll add the class and leave the inline height as is (the CSS sets height:4px, overriding? Inline styles take precedence over classes — the inline `height: "2.4vh"` remains, making the thumb hit area larger — good for UX; but the background #555 from the class will be drawn as a 2.4vh-tall bar (taller than the 4px visual bar) — no good. Remove the background from the input: either add an override class, or set `background: transparent` inline. The simplest: give the input an inline style of background:"transparent" and rely on the class only for the thumb? The class sets height:4px (the inline 2.4vh overrides), background #555 (the inline transparent overrides), border-radius, etc. The thumb styles come from ::-webkit-slider-thumb — unaffected by the inline. So: className "... seek" + add background "transparent" to the style. The thumb will show as a 14px red circle — matches the Netflix look.

Implementing both changes now.

There are 2 changes to make: 1. **Player seek bar**: The range input doesn't have the `seek` class that index.css targets, so the native browser slider appearance ends up showing. Add `seek` to the className, and make sure the inline height doesn't conflict (the CSS's `.seek` sets height 4px + bg #555 — the input's inline style height 2.4vh takes precedence, which makes the clickable area larger. The 4px visual bar is a div behind it, and the input is transparent (bg-transparent)). With the seek class, the thumb becomes a 14px red circle — matches Netflix. Wait, the CSS is `input[type="range"].seek { height: 4px; background: #555 }`. The input already has the `bg-transparent` tailwind class and an inline height of 2.4vh. If I add "seek", the CSS's `background:#555` will conflict with tailwind's `bg-transparent` (same specificity — the utility class and my rule are both single-class selectors. Order matters: index.css is loaded… my rule comes after the tailwind utilities in the same file (after the @tailwind utilities) → the background #555 wins). The input is 2.4vh tall with a #555 background — a chunky 2.4vh gray bar behind the 4px bar — no good. I'll remove `bg-transparent` from the input and instead set an inline `background: "transparent"` (inline > CSS). Keep the seek class for the thumb. Actually, more simply: in index.css, change the seek rule to only style the thumb (the track is handled by the div), and remove the background/height from the base rule. Let me restructure it as follows: ```css input[type="range"].seek { -webkit-appearance:none; appearance:none; background: transparent; } input[type="range"].seek::-webkit-slider-thumb { -webkit-appearance:none; width:14px; height:14px; border-radius:50%; background:#e50914; cursor:pointer; } ``` And in the PlayerPage input: add "seek" to the className. 2. **Continue Watching progress bar**: Home maps cont items: `setCont(cw.ok ? unwrapItems(cw).map((t) => ({ ...t, id: t.title_id })) : [])`. Add `progress_pct: t.progress_seconds && t.duration ? Math.min(98, (t.progress_seconds/t.duration)*100) : null`. In Card, if `title.progress_pct != null`, render a red bar at the bottom of the card (above the hover panel): ```jsx {title.progress_pct != null && (
) ``` Place it inside the media div (before hoverPanel). Apply both.

import re
from collections import Counter
sql = open('app/database/init/02_seed.sql').read()
# episodes: "INSERT INTO episodes (id, title_id, season, number, name, synopsis, duration, thumbnail) VALUES (n, TITLE_ID, S, N, ..."
ep_lines = [l for l in sql.splitlines() if l.startswith("INSERT INTO episodes")]
tg_lines = [l for l in sql.splitlines() if l.startswith("INSERT INTO title_genres")]
ti_lines = [l for l in sql.splitlines() if l.startswith("INSERT INTO titles")]
print("episode lines:", len(ep_lines), "| title_genre lines:", len(tg_lines), "| title lines:", len(ti_lines))
epc = Counter()
for l in ep_lines:
    m = re.match(r"INSERT INTO episodes \(id, title_id, season, number, name, synopsis, duration, thumbnail\) VALUES \(\d+, (\d+), (\d+), (\d+),", l)
    if m: epc[int(m.group(1))] += 1
else:
    pass
series_ids = []
for l in ti_lines:
    m = re.match(r"INSERT INTO titles \(id, name, kind, year, genre, maturity_rating, rating, synopsis, poster, backdrop, video_url, duration, top10_rank, language\) VALUES \((\d+), '([^']*)', '(series|movie)'", l)
    if m and m.group(3) == 'series':
        series_ids.append((int(m.group(1)), m.group(2)))
missing = [t for t in series_ids if t[0] not in epc]
print("series total:", len(series_ids), "series w/o episodes:", len(missing))
print("sample missing:", missing[:5])

raw_content:
Almost everything is clean. There are two trivial leftover artifacts in the backend directory that get copied into the Docker image:
1. `__pycache__/` (4 .pyc files) — harmless, but bloats the Docker build context (it'll get pulled in by `COPY *.py`, no wait — `COPY *.py ./` only copies .py files. The Dockerfile doesn't copy __pycache__. So it only exists in the snapshot).
2. `seed_data.json` — it's referenced by `COPY seed_data.json ./` in the Dockerfile, so it needs to be kept (even though it's unused at runtime).

Delete __pycache__ from the snapshot (it's harmless, but for the sake of cleanliness). Also, check whether .dockerignore is needed in the backend — not needed.

After that, run the final validation and submit.
